subject: Defend-or-Reimburse / Evidence custody — interim compromise proposal
messages:
From: Tom Ellison <t.ellison@archway.bio>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@archway.bio>; Jane Li <jane.li@archway.bio>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Indemnity ask — defend or reimburse + evidence custody

Sofia / Ben —

Thanks for the redlines. Archway legal reviewed the Order Form MSA sections and we need to confirm a few things before we can proceed:

- For third-party IP claims, Archway requires the right to control the defense (including selection of counsel) if the claim relates to our use of the integration; alternatively we will accept a defend-or-reimburse approach where Redwood controls defense but must reimburse Archway for reasonable costs if Archway takes over.
- We need clarification on where technical evidence (logs, model inputs/outputs, audit trails) will live and for how long Redwood will preserve it. Archway will require an evidence export SLA and confirmation that those artifacts can be provided to our counsel on request.
- We have attached our redlines and a short note on escrow vs. short-term preservation.

Can your legal team propose an interim path that gets procurement comfortable to include Redwood in our SOW while we finalize the MSA? Our commercial team is aiming to get this signed in the next 10 business days.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellison
Head of Legal Operations | Archway Bio
Procurement: procurement@archway.bio

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity ask — defend or reimburse + evidence custody

Tom —

Appreciate the quick read. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Ben (AE). We can move to an interim compromise that keeps the deal moving while legal teams finalize MSA language. High-level proposal (see attached Redwood_Interim_Indemnity_Compromise_v1):

1) Right to Defend with Limited Control: Redwood will have the initial right to defend third-party IP claims but Archway may assume control of the defense if Redwood fails to reasonably prosecute or if Archway reasonably believes Redwood's defense conflicts with Archway's material rights.

2) Reimburse Option: If Archway assumes control, Redwood will reimburse Archway for reasonable defense costs incurred after Archway formally notifies Redwood and provides supporting invoices (cap = the policy limit or $5M if uninsured).

3) Evidence Preservation & Export: Redwood will preserve relevant logs, inputs/outputs, and audit trails for 180 days by default and provide an evidence export within 10 business days upon a valid claim notice. For anything older than 180 days, we will work to restore from backups subject to a reasonable retrieval fee.

4) Escrow Trigger & Insurance Offset: As a compromise to escrowing source artifacts, Redwood proposes an escrow activation threshold (claims within 12 months, damages over $250k) and an insurance offset mechanism (to avoid double recovery).

If this high-level compromise sounds workable commercially, Kimberly and Marissa can convert to redline language for the MSA/order form. Ben — can you confirm Archway's procurement timeline and whether they can accept an interim side letter or an amendment to the order form to reflect this compromise?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 13:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity ask — defend or reimburse + evidence custody

Sofia/Kimberly —

Thanks for the calibrated proposal. A few immediate flags from Archway counsel:

- Right to Defend: Our preference remains Archway control for IP claims tied to our product because defense strategy can directly impact downstream regulatory exposure. If Redwood insists on initial control, Archway requires a clearer and shorter transition window to take over (we propose 7 business days after notice) and a commitment that Redwood will not enter into settlement that imposes obligations on Archway without Archway's prior written consent.

- Evidence Preservation: 180 days is borderline for us — we regularly need artifacts for regulatory incident reviews up to 12 months. Can Redwood extend preservation to 12 months for model interaction logs and provide an archival export process?

- Escrow vs. Export: Archway is open to the escrow trigger concept but would prefer a low-friction export-first approach (export + attestations) with escrow as a fallback for high-value claims.

We attach a short counterproposal (redlines embedded). If Redwood can agree to a 12-month preservation window for specified artifact classes and a 7-day takeover window with settlement consent carve-out, we can move procurement forward this week.

On procurement timing: we need a signed Order Form (or amendment) by 2027-07-15 to hit our internal Q3 cutover.

Regards,
Tom

Attachments: Archway_Redlines_20270707.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellison <t.ellison@archway.bio>; Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity ask — defend or reimburse + evidence custody (technical evidence handling)

Tom —

Thanks — Kimberly asked me to handle the technical evidence questions. Quick points and an operational proposal: 

- Artifact classes: we can commit to 12 months preservation for (a) model input/response pairs tied to customer IDs, (b) application-level request/response logs, and (c) system audit trails that directly relate to a claim. We exclude ephemeral inference accelerator traces that are not persisted.

- Export SLA: Redwood can produce an encrypted export package within 10 business days of a valid preservation/export request for artifacts within the 12-month window. Export will include a manifest (we will use the Evidence_Index_Template) and a checksum.

- Temporary Hold vs Escrow: We propose: (1) export-first: Redwood performs export and attestations; (2) if Archway requests escrow, escrow activation occurs only for claims exceeding $250k or where evidence cannot be reconstructed from backups; (3) Redwood will provide a 7-day notice of intent to settle and will not bind Archway without consent.

- Costs: Redwood will absorb preservation and export costs for the first 12 months; retrieval beyond 12 months subject to a fixed retrieval fee (TBD in redline). Insurance offset language will be drafted to prevent double recovery.

I will prepare redline language for the Order Form amendment and share by EOD. If we can agree commercially (Ben/Sofia), we will propose a side letter amendment to be signed ahead of the full MSA redline completion.

—Marissa
